# A step to the self-description (23.8, 23.9): the chain reads words from stdin, looks every word up in
# a dictionary and prints its number, or turns a decimal number into binary. Everything is language 3,
# nothing but lookups, copies, eq and add.
# stdin: words separated by spaces, tabs and line breaks (any byte below 33), the text ends with a zero byte.
# stdout, a line for every word: its number in the dictionary as three decimal digits (000..015),
# "?" when there is no such word, "#" and four hex digits for a decimal number (16 bits, modulo 2^16).
# The dictionary: 16 names of a fixed length, 7 bytes, a name is right-aligned and padded with zero bytes on
# the left (a word of 7 or more bytes can never be found). The word being read moves into a 7-byte buffer
# from the high end, byte after byte; so a word and its dictionary name are compared by eq in 14 nibbles.

# --- the dictionary: the words of the languages 2-4, number 0..15

# --- the character: the byte as it comes (ch, the first bit is the lowest), and as a number (c)

# --- the state of the word being read

# --- the search

# --- the answer

:main block
goto &read

# a byte: the number c from the two nibbles (rev4 turns a nibble of the stream into a number)
:read block
key &ch
lut &rev4 &ch[0:4] &hi
lut &rev4 &ch[4:8] &lo
copy &c[0:4] &lo
copy &c[4:8] &hi
lt &c &k33 &t1
if &t1[2] &sep &chr

# a separator: the word is complete (if there is one); c == 0 ends the text
:sep block
eq &c &k0 &t2
copy &endf &t2[1]
if &has &tok &fin

# a letter: into the buffer from the high end; a digit adds to v = 10 v + digit, any other byte makes bad
:chr block
copy &has &one1
copy &tmp[0:48] &buf[8:56]
copy &tmp[48:56] &ch
copy &buf &tmp
sub &c &k48 &d9
if &d9[8] &nodigit &below
:below block
lt &d9[0:8] &k10 &t3
if &t3[2] &digit &nodigit
:nodigit block
copy &bad &one1
goto &read
:digit block
shl &v &v3 3
shl &v &v1 1
add &v3 &v1 &s17
copy &d16[0:8] &d9[0:8]
add &s17[0:16] &d16 &s17b
copy &v &s17b[0:16]
goto &read

# the word is complete: not only digits, then the search; only digits, then the number
:tok block
if &bad &first &number
:first block
copy &j &z5
goto &look
:look block
lut &dict &j[0:4] &ent
eq &buf &ent &m
if &m[13] &found &next
:next block
lut &add4 &j[0:4] &one4 &zero &j
if &j[4] &miss &look
:found block
lut &dec4 &j[0:4] &dd
copy &out[4:8] &dd[0:4]
copy &out[12:16] &dd[4:8]
copy &out[20:24] &dd[8:12]
emit &out
goto &fin
:miss block
emit &qnl
goto &fin
:number block
lut &hex4 &v[12:16] &hx3
lut &hex4 &v[8:12] &hx2
lut &hex4 &v[4:8] &hx1
lut &hex4 &v[0:4] &hx0
emit &hash
emit &hx3
emit &hx2
emit &hx1
emit &hx0
emit &nl
goto &fin

# the state is cleared for the next word; the end of the text stops
:fin block
copy &has &zero
copy &bad &zero
copy &buf &zb
copy &v &z16
if &endf &done &read
:done block
halt

# 7..0 in a loop with a borrow, print the bytes (progs.array_rev). The values of vals are in the order of
# space (the first bit of a byte is the lowest bit of the number): 130 80 255 0 1 254 200 35.

goto &wr
:wr block

lut &perm &i[0:3] &ix
store &arr &ix &v
lut &add4 &i[0:4] &one &zero &i
lut &lt8 &i[0:4] &c
if &c &wr &rd
:rd block
lut &arr &j[0:3] &o

sub &j &one &jr

if &jr[4] &done &rd
:done block
emit &nl
halt

name: after-l4c-far-serve-at
in:
# Far copy, step 25.4 (7.2.42, 7.2.45): the answerer of far_serve.tw for any position of a window of 1024 cells. A text of language 4: the same protocol over its
# stdin/stdout (the shell connects the stdout of the asker to this stdin and this stdout to the stdin of the asker); the reads and the writes of a cell by its number are
# the computed address of `copy`, `&win@&idx`: not `lut` and `store` but a copy by the value of the cell idx (the pass l4c makes of it the same words of language 3).
# The record of a request: fixed size, 6 bytes, read by three `key`:   op (8 bits)   pos (32 bits)   dat (8 bits)
#   op = 0 (all 8 bits)  stop (no answer)      op = 1  get: answer one byte, win[pos]      op = 2  put: win[pos] = dat (no answer)
#   any other op (3, 4, 16, 255 ...) is a spoiled record: it is skipped, nothing is answered, the next record is read (only op = 0 whole stops the answerer).
#   a number is stored as `key` stores it: the first bit of the stream is the lowest bit (pos: 4 bytes, the lowest byte first).
#   pos is the number of a byte; out of the window (pos >= 1024): get answers a byte of ones (255) = the prohibitive price; put changes nothing.
#   The end of the stdin (the channel is closed) is a stop: op is zeroed before every read and a read at EOF leaves it as it was.
# The window is the array win: 2^10 cells of 8 bits, the largest array of language 3 (K up to 10); the first 8 cells are COPYMACH as in far_serve.tw, the rest are zeros.
# lt works over 8 nibbles (c3 is 9 bits, the test is c3[8]); the index is the 10 low bits of pos (pos[0:10], the width K of the array).

name: after-l4c-packed-far-serve-at
in:

# Far copy, step 25.4 (7.2.42, 7.2.45): the answerer of far_serve.tw for any position of a window of 1024 cells. A text of language 4: the same protocol over its
# stdin/stdout (the shell connects the stdout of the asker to this stdin and this stdout to the stdin of the asker); the reads and the writes of a cell by its number are
# the computed address of `copy`, `&win@&idx`: not `lut` and `store` but a copy by the value of the cell idx (the pass l4c makes of it the same words of language 3).
# The record of a request: fixed size, 6 bytes, read by three `key`:   op (8 bits)   pos (32 bits)   dat (8 bits)
#   op = 0 (all 8 bits)  stop (no answer)      op = 1  get: answer one byte, win[pos]      op = 2  put: win[pos] = dat (no answer)
#   any other op (3, 4, 16, 255 ...) is a spoiled record: it is skipped, nothing is answered, the next record is read (only op = 0 whole stops the answerer).
#   a number is stored as `key` stores it: the first bit of the stream is the lowest bit (pos: 4 bytes, the lowest byte first).
#   pos is the number of a byte; out of the window (pos >= 1024): get answers a byte of ones (255) = the prohibitive price; put changes nothing.
#   The end of the stdin (the channel is closed) is a stop: op is zeroed before every read and a read at EOF leaves it as it was.
# The window is the array win: 2^10 cells of 8 bits, the largest array of language 3 (K up to 10); the first 8 cells are COPYMACH as in far_serve.tw, the rest are zeros.
# lt works over 8 nibbles (c3 is 9 bits, the test is c3[8]); the index is the 10 low bits of pos (pos[0:10], the width K of the array).
